Title: On‑prem L3 policy mismatch — intermittent control‑plane reachability (post‑incident notes)
Summary: This doc captures notes from the on‑call investigation into intermittent control‑plane reachability problems for a handful of on‑prem customers on 2026‑03‑09. Symptoms included sporadic API errors from the private control plane (403/504) and increased reconnection rates observed from agent heartbeats. The underlying issue appeared to be an L3 policy mismatch at customer egress that caused asymmetric routing and conntrack/firewall session drops.
Timeline (local times UTC): - 2026‑03‑09 02:18 — Pager alerts: elevated API 5xx rates reported by internal synthetic checks (region us‑west‑2 private control plane).
- 2026‑03‑09 02:22 — First on‑call triage (Marcus) verifies spike in agent reconnections (heartbeat metric: agent_heartbeat_reconnects increased 8x).
- 2026‑03‑09 02:28 — Errors narrowed to three customer deployments using on‑prem agent v1.9.6 behind customer edge firewalls.
- 2026‑03‑09 02:33 — Remote debugging session with customer A; observed normal control plane health from our side but TCP flows from agents intermittently reset.
- 2026‑03‑09 02:45 — Tomás attaches tcpdump from agent host; shows agent -> control plane SYN/ACK then a RST after ~30s.
- 2026‑03‑09 03:10 — Hypothesis: asymmetric routing / session tracking expiry at customer firewall or NAT device.
- 2026‑03‑09 03:28 — Temporary mitigation: ask customers to add a short keepalive (60s) on the agent side and open a longer conntrack timeout on firewall where possible.
- 2026‑03‑09 05:20 — Observed reduction in reconnection rate from 8x -> 1.3x for mitigated customers.
- 2026‑03‑09 09:00 — Internal post‑incident run (eng + customer network engineer) deeper diagnosis; reproduced by intentionally changing upstream BGP import on customer edge.
Impact: Customers affected: 3 on‑prem deployments; degraded control‑plane API reliability for 20–40% of agent connections during peak of the incident.
User impact: delayed / failed model inference requests that route through affected agents, some automated rollouts delayed.
Duration: ~2.5 hours of elevated error rates; residual low‑level retries for the following day until permanent mitigations applied.
Root cause (current best understanding):
A combination of customer L3 policy and NAT/BGP import policy that caused return traffic for agent TCP sessions to reach a different egress appliance than the one that saw the initial SYN. Customer edge firewall maintained connection state per tuple and dropped replies arriving from the unexpected path (asymmetric flow). This resulted in mid‑session TCP resets or silent drops.
Contributing factors:
- Conntrack/session timeouts on the customer firewall were aggressive for established TCP flows (30s–60s), causing drops when path asymmetry led to delayed replies.
- Agent implementation in v1.9.6 did not send frequent keepalives; idle windows longer than conntrack timeouts amplified the effect.
- BGP import/export policies on customer edge manipulated source addresses for some flows (SNAT) causing tuple mismatches.
Evidence (selected): tcpdump from agent host (timestamp 02:40): SYN -> SYN/ACK -> [no ACK from agent?] then RST when reply came back from different next hop.
conntrack dump provided by customer B showing entries created and aged out at ~35s.
BGP config snippet (customer A) showing conditional next‑hop rewriting for traffic to our control plane IP range.
internal metric: agent_tcp_resets_total spiked 9x during window.
Immediate mitigations taken: Requested customers temporarily increase TCP/session timeouts on edge firewall for flows to Redwood control plane IPs (guidance provided by Priya).
Deployed agent side change (hotfix instruction) to enable keepalive on agent (set keepalive=60s) for affected tenants where on‑call had access to config manager.
Enabled short‑term fallback routing policy on our peering where possible to force symmetric egress for affected customer prefixes (applied on regional peering fabric for 2 customers).
Follow\u2011up / permanent fixes recomme: 1) Product/agent change (prio high): Make TCP keepalive default in agent v1.10 with configurable timeout and exponential backoff. Document runtime flag and include in release notes. Owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026‑03‑23.

2) SRE runbook update (prio medium): Add a dedicated troubleshooting checklist for asymmetric routing / conntrack issues in the Private Control Plane Runbook. Include standard tcpdump/conntrack commands and a customer‑facing template email. Owner: Leah Martinez, ETA: 2026‑03‑16.

3) Networking (prio medium): Add monitoring alert that correlates agent_heartbeat_reconnects with agent_tcp_resets_total and BGP route changes (BGP flaps) to flag possible asymmetric path events. Owner: Marcus Li, ETA: 2026‑03‑30.

4) Solutions Engineering (prio low): For onboarding playbook, include a recommended customer firewall profile for private deployments (conntrack timeout table, NAT behavior, known vendor quirks). Owner: Tomás Rivera, ETA: 2026‑04‑06.
5) Customer outreach: Run brief postmortem calls with affected customers and include configuration recommendations. Owner: Leah Martinez, ETA: 2026‑03‑18.
Runbook fragment \u2014 triage steps (qu:
- Validate symptoms: check agent_heartbeat_reconnects, agent_tcp_resets_total, controlplane_5xx_rate in Observability (last 1h/15m windows).
- Identify affected customers: query agent metadata for failing connection attempts (filter by controlplane IP and customer ID).
- Collect packet captures (ask on‑site customer engineer to run):
    sudo tcpdump -i <iface> host <CONTROL_PLANE_IP> and port 443 -w /tmp/agentcp.pcap
- Check conntrack on customer host (if available):
    sudo conntrack -L | grep <agent_ip> | grep <controlplane_ip>
- On our egress/router: check BGP neighbor flaps and route changes around event window:
    show bgp neighbors | include <peer>
    show route <CONTROL_PLANE_IP>
- Short mitigations to propose to customer:
    - increase established TCP timeout for connections to control plane to >= 300s
    - avoid source NAT rewrite for control plane prefixes (or ensure symmetric path for replies)
    - enable agent keepalive (60s) in config manager
- If customer cannot change firewall, request temporary routing change from their NOC to ensure symmetric path to our control plane (work with SE).

Notes and lessons learned: Asymmetric routing remains a common and subtle failure mode for private/on‑prem customers; small changes in BGP import/export or NAT behavior can surface as control plane reliability issues.
We should treat control plane IP ranges as long‑lived assets in customer network design guidance (advise against rewriting source or next‑hop for these prefixes).
Agent keepalives are cheap and simple; making them default will reduce a large class of connection state timeouts across vendors.
